newsitem.title: UK: Acrylics, viscose depress Courtaulds H1.
newsitem.headline: Acrylics, viscose depress Courtaulds H1.

text.p: Chemicals company Courtaulds Plc said on Wednesday a poor performance by its acrylics and viscose operations was the main factor behind lower first-half profits.
Pretax profit fell to 64.0 million pounds ($107.2 million) from 67.8 million for the six months to September 30, coming in just below analysts' expectations.
While acrylics started a recovery late this summer, margins in viscose have remained inadequate despite signs of orderbook improvement, Courtaulds said.
The profit fall was cushioned by better results for the firm's Tencel fibre, its coatings operations in the Far East and the polymer products.
"Market acceptance of Tencel was again excellent," Courtaulds said in a statement, adding sales nearly doubled compared, while the Tencel business firmly moved into profit.
"The outlook for the second is for further profit profit and turnover growth over the same period last year," the company said.
In polymer products, continuing operations posted 20 percent profit growth. Performance films saw profit move ahead strongly as Far East sales were particularly encouraging.
Packaging sales rose, but profits were held back by the cost of transferring production to new sites in the U.S.
Results in coatings and sealings were boosted by an excellent performance in the Far East where several new products moved to fully commercial production.

"Nothwithstanding the current strength of sterling and the uncertainties surrounding viscose, the group is better positioned now than has been the case for some time," said chief executive Gordon Campbell.
"We have focused on areas where we have real competitive advantage, there is underlying growth in all our key markets and this half has seen improving profits in our core businesses," he added.
